## 1. The form and its first checks

The new-issue page in [new/page.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/app/%28dashboard%29/%5BorgSlug%5D/projects/%5BprojectSlug%5D/issues/new/page.tsx) loads its organization and project through `loadProjectContext()`. That resolves the organization and actor, checks the tenant scope, then loads the project through `getProject()`. Before rendering the form, the page checks `issue:create` permission and counts issues with `includeArchived: true`. If the project is full under the organization’s plan, it shows the full-project message instead.

Otherwise, it passes the project and organization IDs, members, labels, and a validated default status to `IssueForm` in [issue-form.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx). On submit, React Hook Form runs `createIssueSchema` through `zodResolver`; `useFormAction` sets the pending state and calls the supplied `createIssueAction`. The page’s permission and quota checks are useful before submission, but the action repeats the write-critical checks.

The shared schema in [schemas/issue.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/schemas/issue.ts) defines `CreateIssueInput`: title must be 3–200 characters; description is nullable and at most 20,000 characters; status and priority must be recognized enum values; IDs must be ULIDs; estimate must be an integer from 0–100 or null; due date must be an ISO timestamp or null; and there can be at most 20 labels. It supplies defaults for omitted optional fields.

## 2. The Server Action’s gates

`createIssueAction(raw)` in [create-issue.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts) delegates to `withAction()` in [with-action.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts). The wrapper parses the payload with `createIssueSchema` first. Invalid input returns a failed `ActionResult<Issue>` without resolving an actor.

For valid input, `resolveActorFor()` sees `orgId` and calls `requireActorFor()`. That reads the session cookie and resolves its token through [session.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/lib/session.ts) and [session-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/session-service.ts). [actor.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/lib/actor.ts) then resolves the target organization and requires an active membership, producing the `Actor` used by the rest of the server path.

The action calls `can(actor, "issue:create", …)`. In [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/lib/permissions.ts), `issue:create` requires the `member` role, so members, admins, and owners pass; viewers do not. The action then calls `assertProjectHasRoom()`:

- `getOrganizationSummary()` checks `org:read`, and `listIssues()` checks tenant scope and `issue:read`.
- It reads `issuesPerProject` from `getPlanLimits()` in [plan-limits.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/config/plan-limits.ts).
- Its issue count includes archived issues. If `existing.total` is at the limit, it throws `PlanLimitError`.

## 3. Service checks and the database write

Next, `createIssue(actor, input)` in [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/issue-service.ts) repeats core protections: `assertOrgScope()` checks the actor’s tenant; `findProjectById()` loads the project within that organization; `requireFound()` rejects a missing project; `assertNotArchived()` rejects an archived one; and `assertCan()` checks `issue:create` against the loaded project.

The service then loads the organization, counts project issues with `issueRepo.countIssues()`, and applies `wouldExceedLimit()` against the organization’s plan. This is a second quota check, but `countIssues()` uses its default live-only scope, so this service check excludes archived rows; the action’s earlier check is the stricter check because it includes them.

If the checks pass, `nextIssueNumber()` in [issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) takes the maximum number for that organization and project across all rows, including archived ones, then adds one. `insertIssue()` writes the `issues` row with a new ID, that number, the submitted fields, and `actor.userId` as `authorId`; it initializes `startedAt` and `completedAt` to null and stamps `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. The table shape and unique `(projectId, number)` index are in [schema/issues.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/db/schema/issues.ts). If labels were submitted, `insertIssue()` also inserts corresponding `issue_labels` rows, then maps the row to the domain `Issue` type via `toIssue()`.

The schema checks that assignee, parent, and label IDs have ULID shape, but `createIssue()` does not look them up to verify they exist or belong to the same organization. Also, the issue row and label rows are inserted as separate statements, without a transaction around both.

## 4. The `issue.created` consequences

After the database insert, `createIssue()` emits the typed `issue.created` event from [types/event.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/types/event.ts), including the actor envelope, issue and project IDs, title, assignee, and priority. [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/instrumentation.ts) registers the subscribers at server startup through [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/event-registry.ts).

The `issue.created` handlers run concurrently, and `emit()` waits for them all to settle. Their effects are:

- [activity-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/activity-service.ts) records an `activity_events` audit row with the actor, issue, project, title, and priority.
- [search-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/search-service.ts) reloads the issue and upserts a search-index row containing its title and description.
- [usage-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/usage-service.ts) increments the organization’s cached `issuesUsed` count.
- [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) creates pending delivery rows for enabled endpoints subscribed to `issue.created`. A later scheduler or cron run invokes [webhook-delivery-job.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts). In this codebase that job computes and logs a signature, then marks the row delivered; it does not make an outbound HTTP request.

There is no `issue.created` notification subscriber in [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/server/services/notification-service.ts). An assignee set during creation therefore does not, by itself, trigger the assignment notification. The `issue:create` rate-limit bucket is declared in [rate-limit.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/lib/rate-limit.ts), but this create path does not call `consumeRateLimit()`.

## 5. Action response and browser behavior

After `createIssue()` and its event handlers complete, the action invalidates the organization, project, and new-issue cache tags. `withAction()` then invalidates the static `issues` tag and returns a stamped success result. Back in `useFormAction()`, the success callback resets the form and clears its error; on failure, the form displays the returned error message.

One error-mapping detail: Zod validation errors are mapped to `validation_failed`, and service `PermissionDeniedError` is mapped to `forbidden`. However, `toAppError()` in [errors.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/deea9bc5-e7cf-4662-9300-9df506ca9372/src/lib/errors.ts) does not handle the action’s `ForbiddenActionError` or `PlanLimitError`, so those currently fall through to its `internal_error` case.
